clue.text: Birds that have gone with party animals

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
does are female deer, so animals

explanation.surface: Some birds have flown off together with the party crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party animals' looks like one phrase but splits in two; the animals are female deer. DODOES is a less common plural of dodo.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodos are extinct flightless birds, the classic example of a species that has gone for good.

clue.text: The Speaker's skill? Alternatively some MP?

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, so 'alternatively' gives OR
some MP could be a Tory, a Conservative member; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Is public speaking the Speaker's talent, or is it just some MP's?
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs the House of Commons, but here any speaker will do. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, so 'some MP' is one such.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, the skill any orator must have.

clue.text: Nothing charged for Mediterranean fruit

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean fruit is being handed out free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing charged' reads as 'free', but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives grow across the Mediterranean and are botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Mark's weary in the end and chilling

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: the end of the word weary means its last letter only

explanation.surface: Mark is finally worn out and taking it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chilling' looks like relaxing, but it means frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilling makes the blood run cold, which is to say frightening.

clue.text: After function, looks salaciously at online searches

indicators.note: the leering piece comes after the working piece, so it is placed second

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as a machine that will not go
to ogle is to look at someone lecherously

explanation.surface: Once the party is under way, someone leers lewdly at whatever they find online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online searches' is read as a verb: he googles means he searches online.
explanation.definitionFit: To google is to run a web search, from the name of the search engine.

clue.text: Wastes of space seen in 18 and elsewhere in puzzle

definitions.meaning: useless, idle people who contribute nothing

definitions.text: seen in 18 and elsewhere in puzzle
definitions.meaning: read as G (good) for O (nothing): CASINO becomes 18's entry, and other pairs in the grid do the same

explanation.surface: Idle layabouts turn up in one clue and all over the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: G replaces O in pairs of entries, so CASINO turns into CASING, WINO into WING, DODOES into DODGES and GOOGLES into GOGGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Layabouts who are useless to everyone are called worthless people, wastes of space.

clue.text: Bars and courts ridiculously packed in summer time in UK

indicators.note: one piece is crammed into the middle of the other
the word courts is treated absurdly, its letters jumbled into a new order

parts.note: BST stands for British Summer Time

explanation.surface: Pubs and law courts are absurdly crowded during the British summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculously' gives the jumble ORUCTS, and 'packed in' puts the time abbreviation inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar a way is to block or hinder it, a verb sense of the plural 'Bars'.

clue.text: Sounded like oxen — or their burden?

indicators.note: 'or' offers a second reading of 'Sounded like': the entry also sounds like the word for what oxen carry

parts.note: the load an ox pulls is its burden

explanation.surface: Did the oxen moo, or did they sound like the cargo they haul?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounded like' does double duty: it begins the definition, and with 'or' it signals that the entry is said the same as the word for the oxen's burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, meaning they moo, so having mooed they lowed.

clue.text: 15D following English 17

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: 17 down is SOL, which is Spanish and Latin for the sun
the D of 15D is the crossword shorthand for Down

explanation.surface: Nightfall comes after the English sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works twice over: 15D (nightfall) is the definition, while its D read as Down follows SUN, the English for 17's SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is the moment the sun sets, the same thing as nightfall.

clue.text: Seafarers splashing very giant oars

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about like spray, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors are splashing with some very big oars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing' jumbles V with GIANT OARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigators steer ships at sea, so they are mariners.

clue.text: Marginal footballer in debt with no capital

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word is dropped

parts.note: owing money means being in debt

explanation.surface: A fringe player is in debt and has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger plays out on the touchline, so on the margin of the pitch.

clue.text: It's funny to be fetching diamonds for the beginning of Lent

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, as the clue says it is used 'for' it

parts.note: comely means attractive, fetching

indicators.note: only the start of the word Lent is meant, its first letter

parts.note: D is the bridge abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Fetching diamonds at the start of Lent is a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the L of COMELY with D.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a play or film meant to make people laugh.

clue.text: Reveal in advance a lot more food needs cooking

indicators.note: the food has to be prepared, so its letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Plenty more food still has to be cooked, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'plenty' but belongs to the definition: a lot is a fate.
explanation.definitionFit: To foredoom is to fix or foretell someone's fate beforehand, revealing their lot in advance.

clue.text: One of the 28 by ship is cosmetic

parts.note: 28 across is GOGGLES, slang for eyes; one of them is an eye
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: One of a pair of goggles placed by a ship is decorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 28's answer means eyes as well as eyewear, so one of them is EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn around the eyes, a cosmetic product.

clue.text: Regular parts of close-knit garland

indicators.note: letters taken at even intervals, every third one from the second, from the phrase close-knit

explanation.surface: A garland is regularly made of tightly woven pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter, starting with the second: cLosEknIt.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is the Hawaiian flower necklace, a type of floral wreath.

clue.text: Glint half seen flickering in the evening

indicators.note: the light wavers and shifts, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A half-glimpsed glint flickers in the dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flickering' jumbles GLINT HALF.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the start of night, which is the evening.

clue.text: Company adopting adult vice in place of gambling

indicators.note: the company takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A firm takes up an adult vice inside a gaming house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' means the company abbreviation takes the other two pieces inside it. Thematically CASINO becomes 18's entry with G (good) for O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a venue for games of chance such as roulette.

clue.text: Musical note for one singer mostly

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a solo is sung by one singer alone

explanation.surface: A note in the music is meant mainly for a single singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from SOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa, the fifth note of the scale is called sol or soh.

clue.text: About to do karaoke cover?

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
karaoke is singing to a backing track

explanation.surface: Is someone about to cover a song at karaoke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' looks like a cover version for karaoke, but it is an outer shell. Thematically, CASING is CASINO with G (good) for O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A casing is a protective outer shell, something that covers what is inside.

clue.text: Waiting as an enormous row's interrupted

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: the large piece is broken up by the noisy one placed in its middle

parts.note: big means enormous
a din is a row, a noisy racket

explanation.surface: Someone waits while a huge argument is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel or a line, but here it is noise, and "'s interrupted" puts it in the middle of the word for enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is an old word for to wait or stay, so abiding is waiting.

clue.text: Old boy's only travel equipment at first is old hat

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the two words travel and equipment

explanation.surface: A former pupil's only kit for travelling looks dated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Old boy' is just 'has' and joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of date, no longer in use.

clue.text: That place in which to see a bit of tragedy

definitions.text: That place in which to see a bit of tragedy

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside the place named first

parts.note: there means in or at that place

indicators.note: only a small part of tragedy, its first letter, is used

explanation.surface: Here is a venue where you can watch a little tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T go into THERE, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where plays, tragedies included, are staged.

clue.text: Dispose of bath thrown in gully

indicators.note: the bath is tossed into the gully, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a ditch is a gully or trench
Bath is an English spa town, so a spa

explanation.surface: Get rid of the old bath by dumping it in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman spa baths.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch something is to deal with it quickly or kill it, getting rid of it.

clue.text: Fork almost laid flat on top of grill

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed on another, above it
nearly all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: prone means lying face down, laid flat

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fork has almost been laid down flat on the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means above, so the shortened word for lying flat sits over the top letter of 'grill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a spike of a fork, and the word also means a fork or branching.

clue.text: Shellfish might be a different story if ingesting source of effluent

indicators.note: the jumbled letters swallow the other piece, taking it inside
the word story made different, its letters put in another order
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shellfish would be another matter if they swallowed sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' jumbles STORY into OYSTR, and 'ingesting' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc, one of the classic shellfish.

clue.text: Anointed one showed the way starting with love

indicators.note: the whole begins with the tennis zero

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O
I is the Roman numeral for one
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: A holy person, anointed, led the way with love from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a person, but it is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Anointing means smearing with holy oil, so anointed is oiled.

clue.text: Starting price anticipating terminal pay-out

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the other, ahead of it

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
an end is a terminal, the final point

explanation.surface: The starting odds point to a final payment at the betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The starting price is the odds on a horse when a race begins, used to settle bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A spend is an amount of money paid out, an outlay.

clue.text: One down and out to gain nothing

parts.note: to win is to gain
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone destitute stands to gain nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Thematically, WINO turns into 10's WING with G (good) for O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a homeless alcoholic, a figure often seen as down and out.

clue.text: No anther's tip in e.g. poppy without a broken stamen suggests squashings

indicators.note: the clue says there is none of the piece that follows, so it is taken out

parts.note: the field poppy is an annual, a plant that lives one year

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
the remaining letters are broken up and reassembled
the word stamen is taken without the a

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A botany note: a poppy with a broken stamen and no anther tip hints at squashed flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' with 'tip' drops the first A of ANNUAL for ANNUL; 'without' drops the a from STAMEN and 'broken' turns STMEN into MENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment cancels a marriage or ruling; squashing a decision is overturning it.

clue.text: Eyes goods left inside works?

indicators.note: the other pieces are put within the working piece

parts.note: a machine that goes is working
G is short for good, so goods are two Gs

explanation.surface: Someone stares at the merchandise left inside the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goods' is a plural joke: G (good) twice. Thematically, GOGGLES is 5's GOOGLES with G for O.
explanation.definitionFit: To goggle is to stare wide-eyed, so goggles means eyes in the verb sense of looks at.

clue.text: Avoids Western cities?

definitions.meaning: Dodge City is a famous Wild West town in Kansas; the question mark makes it plural

explanation.walkthrough: Thematically, DODGES is 1's DODOES with G (good) for O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade, and Dodge City is an old frontier cattle town in Kansas.
